- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The Occupation authorities abolished the zaibatsu system, which was a group of large, family-owned conglomerates that had dominated the Japanese economy before the war.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Land reform measures were implemented to redistribute land to small farmers and break up large landholdings.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The reforms aimed to promote a more equitable society and stimulate the growth of small businesses.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The Occupation authorities provided economic aid to Japan in the form of loans, technical assistance, and advice on economic policy.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Significant funding was provided for reconstruction projects, including rebuilding factories, infrastructure, and housing.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] These measures helped to revive the Japanese economy and support the growth of small businesses in the postwar era.
